source_text:
ἔχειν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ Θεοῦ κατ' ἰδίαν ὀνομάσας φησὶ μηδὲ
ὀνομαζέσθω ἐν ὑμῖν, εἶτα ἐν ἰδίᾳ χώρᾳ διῃρημένῃ ἀπὸ τῶν προτέρων ἐπήνεγκε τὴν
αἰσχρότητα καὶ μωρολογίαν καὶ εὐτραπελίαν. ἐπειδὴ δὲ ἐν τοῖς ἀνωτέρω
ὑπενοήσαμεν τὴν πλεονεξίαν τετάχθαι ἐπὶ τῆς μοιχείας, ζητῶμεν ἐκ τοῦ ἢ
πλεονέκτης ὅ ἐστιν εἰδωλολάτρης, πότερον ἀνα τρέπεται ἐκείνη ἡ ἐκδοχὴ ἢ ἔτι
δύναται χώραν ἔχειν. εὕρομεν δὴ πολλαχοῦ τῶν προφητῶν τὴν εἰδωλολατρίαν
πορνείαν ὠνομασμένην, ἐν τῷ ἐπόρνευον ὀπί ω τῶν εἰδώλων αὐτῶν. δύναται δέ τις
καὶ τὴν πορνείαν τάξαι ἐπὶ τῆς εἰδωλολατρίας ἐκ τοῦ λέγειν πνεύματι πορνεία
ἐπλανήθη αν. ἐὰν δὲ πλεονέκτης ᾖ ὁ ὅθεν μὴ δεῖ περιποιῶν ἑαυτῷ ἀργύριον,
εἰδωλολατρία λέγεται ἡ πλεονεξία οἱονεὶ λατρευόντων τοῖς ἐγγεγραμμένοις
εἰδώλοις ἐν τοῖς ἀργυρίοις τῶν ἀγαπών των τὸ ἀργύριον, οἱονεὶ γὰρ οὗτοι
συναγαπῶσι τοῖς ἀργυρίοις καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς ἐντετυπωμένα εἴδωλα· οἶμαι δέ που καὶ
τὴν φιλαργυρίαν εἰδωλολατρίαν ὠνομά σθαι παρὰ τῷ ἀποστόλῳ. 25 Eph. v6 [μηδεὶς
ὑμᾶς ἀπατάτω κενοῖς λόγοις, διὰ τοῦτο γὰρ ἔρχεται ἡ ὀργὴ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς
τῆς ἀπειθείας.] [Ὠριγένης φησί] κενοὺς ἔοικε φάσκειν λόγους τοὺς διά τινος
πιθανότητος ἀνατρέπειν θέλοντας τὸν περὶ τῶν προσαγομένων τοῖς κακῶς
βεβιωκόσι κολάσεων λόγον· ἀπάτης γ' οὖν φησιν εἶναι τοὺς τοιούτους λόγους καὶ
κενούς, τῷ πάντως ἔρχεσθαι τὴν λεγομένην ὀργὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς τῆς
ἀπειθείας. ἀπειθείας δὲ υἱοὺς ὀνομάζει τοὺς ἀπειθεῖς, οἱονεὶ τῆς κατὰ τὴν ἀπείθειαν
κακίας μητρὸς γινομένης καὶ γεννώσης αὐτοὺς ἔχοντας οἱονεὶ τὸν τῆς μητρὸς
χαρακτῆρα· οὕτως καὶ υἱοὺς καὶ τέκνα πορνεία καὶ υἱοὺ θανάτου καὶ υἱοὺ γεέννη
καὶ ἄλλα τούτοις παραπλήσιά ἐστι πολλαχοῦ τῶν γραφῶν εὑρεῖν. [v 7] μὴ οὖν
γίνεσθε συμμέτοχοι αὐτῶν. τηρήσεις τὴν «μέτοχος» καὶ «συμμέτοχος» φωνήν·
μήποτε ὁ μὲν μέτοχος ἐπὶ κρείττονος εἴρηται, ὁ δὲ συμμέτοχος ἐπὶ χείρονος, οἷον διὰ
τοῦτο ἔχρι έ ε ὁ θεὸ ὁ θεό ου ἔλαιον ἀγαλλιά εω παρὰ τοὺ μετόχου ου, καὶ
μέτοχοι γὰρ Χρι τοῦ γεγόναμεν, ἐάνπερ τὴν ἀρχὴν τῆ ὑπο τά εω μέχρι τέλου
βεβαίαν κατά χωμεν. οὐ μέμνημαι δὲ ἀλλαχοῦ παρὰ τὴν ἐνεστηκυῖαν λέξιν τὸν
«συμμέτοχον» εἰρῆσθαι, πλὴν φανερὸν ἐνταῦθα ὅτι ἐπὶ χειρόνων ἐστὶν ὁ
συμμέτοχος. [v 8] ἦτε γάρ ποτε σκότος, νῦν δὲ φῶς ἐν Κυρίῳ. εἰ δυνατὸν τὸ ποτὲ
σκότος μεταβαλὸν γενέσθαι φῶς, οὐκ εἰσὶν ἀπολλύμεναι φύσεις. ὥσπερ δὲ οἱ δίκαιοι
φῶ εἰσι τοῦ κό μου, οὕτως οἱ ἀσεβεῖς σκότος ἂν εἶναι λέγοιντο· καὶ οἱ μὲν δίκαιοι
φῶς ὄντες ἐν φωτὶ ὄψονται φῶ , οἱ δὲ ἄδικοι σκότος τυγχάνοντες λαό εἰσι
καθήμενο ἐν κότει μηδὲν βλέποντες. ἀπὸ δὲ τῶν καρπῶν ἐπιγνω όμεθα τοὺς ὄντας
φῶς ἢ σκότος· πᾶ μὲν γὰρ ὁ φαῦλα πρά ων μι εῖ τὸ φῶ , καὶ μὴ ἐρχόμενο πρὸ τὸ
φῶ σκότος ἐστὶ καὶ υἱὸς σκότους καὶ νυκτός· ὁ δὲ ποιῶν τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἐρχόμενο
πρὸ τὸ φῶ φῶς ἐστι καὶ υἱὸς φωτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας. πρὸς τούτοις ἐπιστήσεις εἰ μὴ ὡς
ὄντων τινῶν φώτων ἀλλ' οὐκ ἐν κυρίῳ λέγεται περὶ τῶν δικαίων τὸ νῦν δὲ φῶς ἐν
κυρίῳ· καὶ μάλιστά γε τοῖς πεφω τισμένοις ἐν φωτὶ γνώσεως Ἐφεσίοις ἔπρεπε
λέγεσθαι τὸ νῦν δὲ φῶς ἐν κυρίῳ. [v 8] ὡς τέκνα φωτὸς περιπατεῖτε. εἴπερ ὁ Θεὸ
φῶ ἐ τι καὶ κοτία ἐν αὐτῷ οὐκ ἐ τὶν οὐδεμία, τὰ τέκνα τοῦ Θεοῦ τέκνα ἐστὶ φωτός.
[v 9] ὁ γὰρ καρπὸς τοῦ φωτὸς ἐν πάσῃ ἀγαθωσύνῃ καὶ δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ. πρὸς
τοὺς διαχωρίζοντας τὸν δίκαιον ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ, καὶ οἰομένους τὸν μὲν δημιουργὸν
εἶναι δίκαιον ὃν δὲ οἴονται ὑπὲρ αὐτὸν ἀγαθὸν Θεόν, χρήσιμα τὰ ῥητά· ἐπείπερ ὁ τοῦ
φωτὸς καρπὸς καὶ ἐν ἀγαθωσύνῃ ἐστὶ καὶ ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ. ὅπου οὖν
ἀγαθωσύνη ἐκεῖ δικαιοσύνη, καὶ ὅπου ἀλήθεια ἐκεῖ δικαιοσύνη. παρὰ δὲ τῷ ἀγαθῷ
πατρὶ ἀγαθωσύνη καὶ ἀλήθεια· παρ' αὐτῷ ἄρα καὶ οὐ παρ' ἄλλῳ ἐστὶν ἡ δικαιοσύνη.
pass_a_gloss: ... to have in the kingdom of Christ and of God, having named them separately he says "let it not even be named among you"; then in a place of its own divided off from the former ones he brought in shamefulness and foolish talk and jesting. But since in the things above we suspected that greed has been set for adultery, let us seek from the phrase "or greedy person, which is an idolater" whether that interpretation is overturned or is still able to have room. Indeed we found in many places of the prophets idolatry named fornication, in "they were committing fornication behind their idols." And someone can also set fornication for idolatry, from its saying "by a spirit of fornication they were led astray." And if the greedy man is the one gaining money for himself from where he must not, greed is called idolatry as of people worshipping the idols inscribed on the silver coins of those who love silver; for these, as it were, love together with the coins also the idols impressed on them. And I suppose that somewhere love of money too has been named idolatry by the apostle. Eph 5:6 lemma: let no one deceive you with empty words, for on account of this the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience. [Origen says] He seems to say that empty words are those wishing through some plausibility to overturn the account concerning the punishments applied to those who have lived badly; at any rate he says such words are of deceit and empty, by the fact that the said wrath of God altogether comes upon the sons of disobedience. He names the disobedient sons of disobedience, as if the vice of disobedience became a mother and begot them having as it were the mother's stamp; so also sons and children of fornication and sons of death and sons of Gehenna and other things close to these can be found in many places of the writings. Eph 5:7: do not then become co-partakers of them. You will observe the word "partaker" and "co-partaker"; perhaps the partaker is said of the better, and the co-partaker of the worse, for instance "on account of this God your God anointed you with oil of gladness beyond your partakers", and "for we have become partakers of Christ, if indeed we hold the beginning of the confidence firm until the end". I do not recall elsewhere besides the present phrase "co-partaker" being said, except it is plain here that the co-partaker is of worse things. Eph 5:8: for you were once darkness, but now light in the Lord. If it is possible for the once-darkness, having changed, to become light, there are not natures that are perishing. And as the righteous are light of the world, so the impious might be said to be darkness; and the righteous, being light, in light will see light, but the unjust, being darkness, are a people sitting in darkness seeing nothing. From the fruits we shall recognize those being light or darkness: for everyone doing base things hates the light, and not coming to the light is darkness and a son of darkness and night; but the one doing the truth, coming to the light, is light and son of light and of day. Toward these you will consider whether, as of there being some lights but not in the Lord, the "but now light in the Lord" is said about the righteous; and most of all it fitted the Ephesians, enlightened in a light of knowledge, to be told "but now light in the Lord". Eph 5:8b: walk as children of light. If God is light and there is no darkness in him at all, the children of God are children of light. Eph 5:9: for the fruit of the light is in all goodness and justice and truth. Toward those dividing the just from the good and supposing the craftsman to be just but the one whom they suppose above him the good God, the sayings are useful; since the fruit of the light is both in goodness and in justice and in truth. Therefore where goodness, there justice, and where truth, there justice. But with the good Father are goodness and truth; with him then and not with another is the justice.
pass_b_english: to have in the kingdom of Christ and God, he names on their own, and says, "Let it not even be named among you." Then, in a place of its own, set apart from the earlier ones, he adds shamefulness, foolish talk and coarse joking.

Earlier we supposed that "greed" was put for adultery. So let us ask, from the words "or a greedy person, who is an idolater," whether that reading is overturned or can still stand. Now we have found that in many places the prophets call idolatry fornication, as in "they went whoring after their idols." And one could also take fornication to stand for idolatry, from the saying, "By a spirit of fornication they went astray" (Hosea 4:12). But if the greedy person is the one who gets money for himself from where he ought not, greed is called idolatry because those who love money are, as it were, worshipping the images engraved on the coins; for along with the coins these people love, as it were, the images stamped on them too. And I think the apostle somewhere also calls the love of money idolatry.

"Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of this the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience" (Ephesians 5:6). Origen says: He seems to call "empty words" the words that try, by some show of persuasion, to overturn the teaching about the punishments brought on those who have lived wickedly. At any rate he says that such words belong to deceit and are empty, because the wrath of God spoken of here will certainly come upon the sons of disobedience. He calls the disobedient "sons of disobedience," as though the vice of disobedience became a mother and bore them, so that they carry, as it were, their mother's likeness. In the same way one can find in many places of the Scriptures "sons" and "children of fornication," "sons of death," "sons of Gehenna" and other phrases like these.

"Do not, then, become fellow partakers with them" (Ephesians 5:7). Note the words "partaker" and "fellow partaker." Perhaps "partaker" is said of the better and "fellow partaker" of the worse. So, for example: "Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your partakers" (Psalm 45:7), and, "For we have become partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence firm to the end" (Hebrews 3:14). I do not remember "fellow partaker" being used anywhere except in the present passage; but here it is clear that the fellow partaker belongs to the worse.

"For you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord" (Ephesians 5:8). If what was once darkness can change and become light, there are no natures doomed to perish. Just as the righteous are the light of the world, so the ungodly might be called darkness. The righteous, being light, will see light in light; but the unjust, being darkness, are a people sitting in darkness, seeing nothing. By their fruits we shall recognize who is light and who is darkness. For everyone who does evil hates the light, and, not coming to the light, he is darkness, a son of darkness and of night; but whoever does the truth comes to the light, and he is light, a son of light and of day (John 3:20-21). Besides this, consider whether "but now you are light in the Lord" is said of the righteous because there are some lights that are not in the Lord. It was especially fitting that the Ephesians, enlightened in the light of knowledge, should be told, "but now you are light in the Lord."
"Walk as children of light" (Ephesians 5:8). If God is light and there is no darkness in him at all, then the children of God are children of light.

"For the fruit of the light is in all goodness and justice and truth" (Ephesians 5:9). These words are useful against those who separate the just from the good, and who think that the Creator is just, but that the one they imagine above him is the good God. For the fruit of the light is in goodness and in justice and in truth. Where there is goodness, then, there is justice; and where there is truth, there is justice. But goodness and truth are with the good Father; so justice too is with him and not with another.

choices.why: The catena label stands in the Greek (editor's brackets); rendered as in u01-u04.
Origen's argument turns on δίκαιος (the 'just' God of his opponents) and δικαιοσύνη; 'justice' keeps the link visible in English.

choices.english: there are no natures doomed to perish
choices.why: Against a fixed class of perishing natures; 'doomed' renders the present participle of a state, not an added claim.

choices.term: πρὸς τοὺς διαχωρίζοντας ... χρήσιμα τὰ ῥητά
choices.english: These words are useful against those who separate...
choices.why: Full sentence as in the Greek; no heading-like label.
